reviewed: Read all four pre-existing dry-eye foundations rows and embedded check; NEI supports basic mechanisms, exposures, diagnosis and care. Detailed medicine/systemic-disease list still needs dedicated source verification.
Read all sterility lesson rows and embedded check. FDA supports sterility, tip hygiene, alert review and unapproved-product cautions. Lens-water guidance remains to be reconciled against CDC.
CDC supports existing no-water lens guidance; expanded concrete care instructions. Existing lens visual describes exact-label removal and no-wear plan and remains consistent.

Reconciled detailed medication and systemic-disease risk list with NEI and TFOS report passages. Anticholinergic mechanism, antihistamine/diuretic and benzodiazepine associations, isotretinoin gland effects, Parkinson-related blink impairment and dermatologic MGD associations support contextual evaluation. Epidemiologic association does not establish individual causation.

Pediatric triage row and questions 121–124 agree with RCH acute-red-eye assessment guidance. Read pregnancy/lactation questions 125–128; current product labels support individualized risk assessment, with systemic-exposure reduction supported by AAO journal search-indexed passages (full-text request failed). Administration accessibility remains a practical counseling synthesis, not a quantified efficacy claim.

Administration rows and embedded check reconciled with reviewed product IFUs and trial abstract: clean hands, lower-lid sac, tip clearance, prescribed drop count, gentle closure/occlusion, exact-product spacing and thicker preparations last. Existing text makes no universal exposure-reduction percentage or pregnancy safety guarantee. Special-population row retains product-specific benefit-risk review; source reconciliation closed for the general claims actually taught.
